header.passionateDeveloper: Passionate developer with over 10 years of experience and a focus on modern web technologies.
header.transform: I transform ideas into elegant, functional solutions.

about.text1: I have been creating websites since my youth and have gained experience with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and PHP.
about.text2: In 2019, I laid the foundation for a professional career in web and mobile app development through targeted online courses, specializing in Angular and Ionic.
about.text3: In the course of my professional career, I have continuously expanded my knowledge and also learned backend programming with the Node.js framework NestJS, which I use in various projects.
about.text5: Since then, I have been working as a freelancer and supporting various companies. My focus is on the development and further development of complex websites and mobile applications.
about.text6: German is my native language. I am also fluent in English and have advanced knowledge of Croatian.
about.text7: I am married and the proud father of one child.
about.sectionH:
Specialized in modern web and app development
with a focus on performance.
about.spec: Specialized in modern web and app development with a focus on performance.
about.p1: Over ten years of experience in software development have taught me one thing: code is only half the battle. It's about understanding problems, questioning requirements, and delivering solutions that are still maintainable two years from now.
about.p2: Currently I work on frontends with Angular and Ionic as well as backends with NestJS — from internal dashboards to production mobile apps with thousands of users.
about.p3: Clean code, clear component structure, tested with Cypress. If you're interested in what's between the lines: check out the projects or get in touch directly.

orbit.title: Orbit
orbit.subtitle: A 3D model of the solar system. Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, click a world for its file.
orbit.hintKeys: Space pause · Esc back · R overview · L names · O orbits
orbit.credit: Textures: NASA / Solar System Scope (CC BY 4.0). Distances and sizes are compressed so Earth is not a single pixel.

sun.name: Sun
sun.blurb: The furnace at the centre. More than 99 percent of the system's mass, a boiling sphere of hydrogen and helium.
sun.fact: A photon takes millennia to crawl out of the core — then eight minutes to reach Earth.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.blurb: Smallest and fastest. A cratered world with almost no air, scorching on the day side, frozen at night.
mercury.fact: A Mercury day lasts two Mercury years. Sunrise, sunset, sunrise again — then midnight.

venus.name: Venus
venus.blurb: Earth's twin in size, otherwise the opposite: choking CO₂, sulphuric clouds, a greenhouse with no mercy.
venus.fact: It spins backwards, so slowly that a day lasts longer than a year.

earth.name: Earth
earth.blurb: The pale blue dot. Liquid water, a breathable sky, and at night a net of cities — the only home we know.
earth.fact: Axial tilt makes the seasons. Without the Moon, the axis would wobble wildly.

moon.name: Moon
moon.blurb: Born in a collision, locked in sync: we always see the same face.
moon.fact: It recedes by about 3.8 cm each year — Earth's day grows longer with it.

mars.name: Mars
mars.blurb: Rust-red from iron oxide. Thin air, giant volcanoes, ice caps — the next place for footprints.
mars.fact: Olympus Mons is the tallest volcano in the solar system — nearly three Everests stacked.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.blurb: A failed star: hydrogen, helium, a storm larger than Earth. Its gravity keeps the inner system in line.
jupiter.fact: The Great Red Spot has raged for at least 350 years. A day lasts under ten hours.

io.name: Io
io.blurb: The most volcanic world we know. Jupiter's tides knead it; sulphur paints the crust orange and yellow.
io.fact: Hundreds of volcanoes, some plumes hundreds of kilometres high. No craters — the crust keeps renewing.

europa.name: Europa
europa.blurb: An ice shell over an ocean. Under the frost, probably more water than in all of Earth's seas.
europa.fact: One of the hottest bets for life beyond Earth — not on the ice, but under it.

ganymede.name: Ganymede
ganymede.blurb: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than Mercury, with its own magnetic field.
ganymede.fact: Ice and rock in layers, and likely a saltwater ocean underneath.

callisto.name: Callisto
callisto.blurb: The most cratered face in the system. Little tidal heat, an ancient crust almost unchanged.
callisto.fact: Outside the main radiation belt — which is why it is a serious candidate for a future base.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.blurb: Light enough to float on water, famous for an ice ring system you can see from here.
saturn.fact: The rings are only tens of metres thick, yet wider than the Earth–Moon gap.

titan.name: Titan
titan.blurb: Denser air than Earth, methane lakes, orange haze. A frozen version of a young Earth.
titan.fact: The Huygens probe landed in 2005 — still the most distant touchdown in history.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.blurb: A planet on its side. The poles point almost into the orbital plane; seasons last for decades.
uranus.fact: The extreme tilt likely comes from an ancient collision — ever since, it rolls along its path.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.blurb: The outermost planet, deep blue from methane, with the fastest winds we know.
neptune.fact: Since its discovery in 1846 it finished its first orbit only in 2011.
